subject: Dedicated capacity guarantees: tokens/sec & latency validation plan
messages:
From: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@nimbus.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nimbus.ai, Asha Patel <asha.patel@nimbus.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:05:12 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool guarantees — initial ask

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our infra/product teams want specific guarantees tied to a Dedicated GPU pool so we can finalize the procurement sheet. Primary asks:
- Target sustained tokens/sec (for our 512-token average completions).
- Target requests/sec (concurrent inference requests).
- Latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) by request type and sequence length.
- How you propose to measure and validate these guarantees pre- and post-commit.

We're targeting ~650 requests/sec peak with an average of 320 tokens per request across a mixed chat+completion workload (roughly 60/40 split). Curious how you map that to GPU pool sizing and what credit/SLR you provide if you fall short.

Can you share a measurement methodology we can review internally? Procurement also wants a 30–90 day validation window defined.

Jordan
Jordan Matthews
Head of ML Ops, Nimbus AI
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@nimbus.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 16:23:48 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool guarantees — initial ask

Jordan —

Appreciate the concrete numbers, that helps. Attached is a first-draft validation plan (RBW-Dedicated-Throughput-Method-v1.pdf) that spells out measurement harness, sampling methodology, and acceptance criteria. High level summary here so procurement has something concise: 

- Tokens/sec vs requests/sec: We characterize both. For your profile we translate 650 rps * 320 tokens -> theoretical token throughput target. In practice we size GPU pool for headroom (typical sizing is 1.3–1.6x expected steady-state token/sec depending on prompt distribution and KV-cache hit rate).
- Latency SLOs: We propose p50/p95/p99 for 1..512 token completions. Example goals: p50 < 40ms per token (streamed), p95 < 200ms per token, request-level p95 for 512-token completion < 2s. We’ll finalize benchmarks against your exact prompts.
- Measurement methodology: 30-min warm-up, run three 1-hour test blocks over a simulated production traffic mix. Measure rolling 5-min windows; acceptance is that >=95% of 5-min windows meet token/sec target and p95 latency target during the validation period.
- Validation window: Default 30 days (production), but procurement can require an initial 14-day on-prem soak followed by 30-day post-cutover measurement.

Pricing/discount tie-ins: commitments (3/6/12-month) map to progressive discounts; failure credits are pro-rated for under-delivery weeks (details in the attached).

If you want, we can set up a joint measurement run next week — our SE Lauren can own the harness.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: RBW-Dedicated-Throughput-Method-v1.pdf (PDF, 38KB)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@nimbus.ai>, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:12:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool guarantees — initial ask

Jordan / team —

Looping in a few practical clarifications from SE side based on common pitfalls:

- Prompt distribution: measurement must use a sampled prompt set from your logs (we recommend 1k unique prompts stratified by token length and call type). If you can share anonymized samples we will run an identical workload.
- Cold-start vs steady-state: we report both. Guarantees apply to steady-state (after 30-min warm-up) but we also provide cold-start windows so you know tail behavior.
- KV cache: your 60/40 split implies significant prefix reuse. We’ll run two modes: cache-disabled (worst-case) and cache-enabled (expected). Guarantees are for the expected (cache-enabled) but procurement can choose conservative guaranteed levels tied to cache-disabled runs.
- Measurement harness: we use a hybrid of k6 + internal runtime probes to capture per-token emission latencies. Request-level p95 is derived from end-to-end wall time including ingress/egress.

Operational ask: can your infra team open a temporary VPC peering and provide an IP allowlist for the test driver?

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the attached doc.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@nimbus.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@nimbus.ai>, procurement@nimbus.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 08:03:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool guarantees — initial ask

Lauren — thanks, that's helpful. We can provide a 1k-sample prompt set (anonymized) and we'll coordinate with infra about a test CIDR for peering. Procurement wants the validation plan baked into the SOW with explicit credit triggers and an escalation path. Two specific asks from the procurement side: 

1) If committed throughput is missed for >3 non-consecutive weeks in a rolling 90-day period, we want a service credit of 10% of that month's reserved fee.
2) We need a clear measurement adjudication process (who owns the metric logs, how disputes are resolved).

Can your legal/ops folks draft the SOW language? Once we have that procurement will push a redline.

Jordan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 09:45:50 -0700
Subject: Internal: measurement adjudication proposal

Internal note — proposed objective measurement/adjudication flow to include in SOW: 

- Shared telemetry: Redwood will stream anonymized aggregate telemetry (5-min bins) to a shared S3 bucket for the validation window. Bucket ACL permits read-only access to Nimbus procurement and engineering.
- Audit logs: we export per-request hashes + timestamp (no payload) for dispute resolution (retention 90 days).
- Dispute process: 72-hour triage window where both sides exchange evidence; independent 3rd-party measurement (optional, paid by the losing party) if unresolved.
- Credits: map to the same week’s reserved commit; cap at 30% of monthly reserved fee per 30-day period.

Also, for latency targets we should define canonical sequence lengths for reporting: 64, 128, 256, 512 tokens and report p50/p95/p99 for each. For tokens/sec, use rolling 5-min windows and report both mean and 95th percentile across the validation window.

Karthik
Product Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@nimbus.ai>, procurement@nimbus.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool guarantees — initial ask

Jordan / Asha / procurement team —

Thanks — this is actionable. Next steps we propose: 
1) Redwood and Nimbus agree on exact prompt sample and traffic mix (aditya to collect sample by EOD Tue).
2) Redwood runs an initial 3-hour validation and shares raw 5-min binned telemetry + summary (within 48 hours).
3) If initial run passes, we proceed to a 30-day soak as defined in the attached SOW draft. If it fails, we iterate sizing or commit level before moving to the soak.

On discounts: our standard reserved-commit tiers for this class of pool are: 3-month (12% discount), 6-month (18%), 12-month (25%). We can make the 12-month tier contingent on a final production run and offer a one-time onboarding credit if the 30-day validation is delayed beyond 45 days.

I'll ask legal/ops to prepare SOW language aligned with Karthik's adjudication flow and the procurement credit asks.

Are you available for a 30-min mapping call Wed 9/15 at 10am PT?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: Nimbus-MAP-draft.xlsx (XLSX, 14KB)
